title: Pack the assets for Ada
prompt:
Ada needs Mira’s game assets for the 0.9 build, as one compressed file she can download.

In Mira’s home directory, pack the folder `assets` into a tar archive named `assets-0.9.tar.bz2`, compressed with bzip2. The archive must hold the folder itself, so that unpacking it creates `assets/`.
hints: `tar` creates an archive with `-c` and names the archive file with `-f`. Another option picks the compression.
`-z` is gzip, `-j` is bzip2 and `-J` is xz.
Give `tar` the folder name, `assets`, not the files inside it, so the paths in the archive start with `assets/`.
check:
f=assets-0.9.tar.bz2
if [ ! -f "$f" ]; then no "There is no $f in Mira’s home directory yet."; exit 1; fi
ok "$f exists."
if file -b "$f" | grep -q '^bzip2'; then ok "It is compressed with bzip2."; else no "It isn’t compressed with bzip2: file says “$(file -b "$f")”."; fi
if tar -tf "$f" 2>/dev/null | grep -qx 'assets/sprites/hero.png'; then ok "It holds the assets folder, with paths starting at assets/."; else no "It doesn’t hold assets/sprites/hero.png. Pack the folder assets itself."; fi

title: Unpack into a separate folder
prompt:
Mira wants to compare her `assets` folder with the archive `assets-0.9.tar.gz` without overwriting anything.

Create a folder `restore` in her home directory and unpack `assets-0.9.tar.gz` into it, so that the files end up in `restore/assets/…`.
hints: `tar -x` extracts; `-z` reads gzip; `-f` names the archive. `tar -tzf` lists the contents first, without extracting.
By default `tar` extracts into the current directory. The option `-C` changes into another directory first.
check:
if [ -d restore ]; then ok "~/restore exists."; else no "There is no folder ~/restore yet."; exit 1; fi
if [ -f restore/assets/levels/level1.txt ] && cmp -s restore/assets/sprites/hero.png assets/sprites/hero.png; then ok "The archive is unpacked in restore/assets."
else no "restore/assets/levels/level1.txt isn’t there. Unpack the archive inside restore."; fi
if [ ! -e restore/restore ] && [ ! -e assets/assets ]; then ok "Nothing was unpacked in the wrong place."; else no "Some files were unpacked in the wrong place."; fi

title: A zip file for the level designer
prompt:
A freelance level designer works on Windows and asks for the level files as a `.zip`.

Create `levels.zip` in Mira’s home directory, holding the folder `assets/levels` and everything in it.
hints: The tool is called `zip`. Its first argument is the archive to create, then the files to put in.
Like `cp`, `zip` needs `-r` to include a folder with what is inside it.
`zip -r levels.zip assets/levels`, then check with `unzip -l levels.zip`.
check:
if [ ! -e levels.zip ]; then no "There is no levels.zip yet. Create it in Mira’s home directory."; exit 1; fi
ok "levels.zip exists."
if file -b levels.zip | grep -q '^Zip archive'; then ok "It is a zip archive."; else no "It isn’t a zip archive: file says “$(file -b levels.zip)”."; exit 1; fi
if unzip -l levels.zip | grep -q 'assets/levels/level1.txt'; then ok "It holds assets/levels/level1.txt."; else no "It doesn’t hold assets/levels/level1.txt. Did you add the folder with -r?"; fi
